newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Another 18 people were arrested by the Independent Commission Against Corruption in the investigation into alleged syndicated race-fixing. The total number of people arrested came to 37.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Beijing sources said former Chinese President Zhao Ziyang had written to the top leadership earlier this year expressing his views on political and economic reforms, setting up a democratic system within the Party, and allowing revolutionary humanitariansm.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- A Taiwanese company is likely to take control of Hong Kong-based Chinese Television Network after acquiring over 50 percent of its shares, moving its headquarters to Taiwan and replacing managing director Yu Pun-hoi.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- At the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group meeting in London, the British side will try to reach and agreement with China over the definition of "permanent residents" in Hong Kong.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Democratic Party leader Martin Lee said after meeting Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa that he would continue speaking the truth overseas about Hong Kong. Tung had asked the Democrats to express their views with care.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Prime Minister John Major ended months of speculation by announcing that the British general election would take place on May 1, Labour Day.
-- Cheung Kong (Holdings) was embarking on an aggressive selling spree, releasing two major residential projects in consecutive weeks to tap the bullish market.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- China was prohibiting mainlanders from visiting Hong Kong for travel purposes during the handover in a move aimed at increasing stability in the territory during the historic period.
